# Parse the old songs file content to extract song titles and artists
import re

content = old_songs_file['content']
songs = []
for line in content.split('\n'):
    line = line.strip()
    if line.startswith('- '):
        # Remove the leading "- "
        song_str = line[2:]
        # Split on " by " to get title and artists
        if ' by ' in song_str:
            title, artists_str = song_str.split(' by ', 1)
            artists = [a.strip() for a in artists_str.split(',')]
            songs.append({'title': title.strip(), 'artists': artists})
        else:
            songs.append({'title': song_str.strip(), 'artists': []})

print(songs)

        parts = song_part.rsplit(' by ', 1)

else:

# Parse the old songs list from the file content.
import re

content = fs_file['content']
lines = content.strip().split('\n')
old_songs = []
for line in lines:
    line = line.strip()
    if line.startswith('#') or not line:
        continue
    # Format: "- Title by Artist1, Artist2"
    if line.startswith('- '):
        line = line[2:]
    # Split on " by " (last occurrence)
    if ' by ' in line:
        title_part, artists_part = line.rsplit(' by ', 1)
        title = title_part.strip()
        artists = [a.strip() for a in artists_part.split(',')]
        old_songs.append({'title': title, 'artists': artists})
    else:
        # maybe just title?
        old_songs.append({'title': line.strip(), 'artists': []})

steps.code:
# Let's compute the set of target song_ids and then process each playlist.
target_song_ids = set(song_ids.values())
print("Target song IDs:", target_song_ids)

# We'll track which songs have been added to the new playlist to avoid duplicates
added_to_new = set()

# Iterate over each playlist
for pl in playlists:
    pl_id = pl['playlist_id']
    pl_song_ids = pl['song_ids']
    # Find songs in this playlist that are in target set
    to_remove = [sid for sid in pl_song_ids if sid in target_song_ids]
    if to_remove:
        print(f"Playlist {pl_id} ({pl['title']}) has songs to remove: {to_remove}")
        for sid in to_remove:
            # Remove from this playlist
            remove_res = apis.spotify.remove_song_from_playlist(playlist_id=pl_id, song_id=sid, access_token=spotify_login['access_token'])
            print(f"  Removed song {sid} from playlist {pl_id}: {remove_res}")
            # Add to new playlist if not already added
            if sid not in added_to_new:
                add_res = apis.spotify.add_song_to_playlist(playlist_id=654, song_id=sid, access_token=spotify_login['access_token'])
                print(f"  Added song {sid} to new playlist: {add_res}")
                added_to_new.add(sid)
    else:
        print(f"Playlist {pl_id} ({pl['title']}) has no songs to remove.")

print("Songs added to new playlist:", added_to_new)

    pl_title = pl["title"]
    present = [sid for sid in pl["song_ids"] if sid in archive_song_ids]
    if present:
        print(f"Playlist '{pl_title}' (id={pl_id}) has archive songs: {present}")
        for sid in present:
            result = apis.spotify.remove_song_from_playlist(playlist_id=pl_id, song_id=sid, access_token=spotify_token)
            print(f"  Removed song {sid}: {result}")
    else:
        print(f"Playlist '{pl_title}' (id={pl_id}) has no archive songs.")

# All archive songs removed from their playlists. Now create the new playlist "Archived Playlist Songs".

# Define the set of target song IDs to archive.
target_song_ids = {295, 324, 22, 245, 320, 92, 299, 4, 278, 69, 219, 298, 265}
new_playlist_id = 654
added_songs = set()  # to avoid duplicates in new playlist

# Iterate over all playlists
for pl in playlists:
    pl_id = pl['playlist_id']
    # Get playlist details to see its songs
    pl_data = apis.spotify.show_playlist(playlist_id=pl_id, access_token=spotify_token)
    songs = pl_data.get('songs', [])
    for song in songs:
        song_id = song['id']
        if song_id in target_song_ids:
            # Remove from this playlist
            print(f"Removing song {song_id} from playlist {pl_id}")
            apis.spotify.remove_song_from_playlist(playlist_id=pl_id, song_id=song_id, access_token=spotify_token)
            # Add to new playlist if not already added

    if line.startswith('- '):
        # Extract title and artists
        # Format: - Title BY Artist1, Artist2 RELEASED_AT TODO
        # Use regex to capture title and artists
        m = re.match(r'- (.+) BY (.+) RELEASED_AT (TODO|\d{2}/\d{4})', line)

            if release == 'TODO':

    # We'll replace "RELEASED_AT TODO" with "RELEASED_AT {release}" for that specific line
    # To be safe, we'll replace only the first occurrence of "RELEASED_AT TODO" after the title
    # But since each title is unique, we can just replace the whole line.
    # We'll split content into lines, process each line.
    pass

# Let's do it properly by processing lines
lines = content.split('\n')
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract the song title from the line
        # Format: "- {title} BY {artists} RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # We'll find the title between "- " and " BY "
        if line.startswith('- '):
            # Find " BY " to get title
            title_part = line[2:].split(' BY ')[0]
            if title_part in release_map:
                line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', 'RELEASED_AT ' + release_map[title_part])
    new_lines.append(line)

steps.code:
# Build the mapping of song titles to release month/year
release_dates = {
    "Lost in the Embrace of Night": "03/2021",
    "Lonely Skies": "11/2022",
    "Caught in a Web of Lies": "03/2021",
    "On the Border of Reality": "08/2022",
    "A Love That Never Was": "10/2020",
    "Astral Serenity": "12/2019",
    "Between Reality and Reverie": "03/2020",
    "Strangers Again": "06/2022",
    "The Mirage of a Perfect Life": "11/2020",
    "Wilted Roses on the Vine": "02/2020",
    "When All Words Fail Us": "07/2020",
    "Final Echo": "07/2022"
}

# Get the note content
note_content = note['content']

# Split into lines
lines = note_content.split('\n')

# Process each line
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title: line starts with "- " then title, then " BY "
        # Example: "- Lost in the Embrace of Night BY Noah Bennett RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # We'll find the part between "- " and " BY "
        # Use split
        parts = line.split(' BY ')
        # parts[0] is "- Song Title", parts[1] is "Artist(s) RELEASED_AT TODO"
        song_title = parts[0][2:]  # remove "- "
        # Get the release date
        release = release_dates.get(song_title)
        if release is None:
            print(f"Warning: No release date for {song_title}")
            new_lines.append(line)  # keep as is
        else:
            # Replace the TODO with the release date
            new_line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', f'RELEASED_AT {release}')
            new_lines.append(new_line)
    else:
        new_lines.append(line)

# Join back
new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)

# Print the new content to verify
print(new_content)

# Parse the note content to extract TODO songs
note_content = note['content']
lines = note_content.split('\n')
todo_songs = []
for line in lines:
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title and artist part
        # Format: "- Song Title BY Artist1, Artist2 RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Remove leading "- " and trailing " RELEASED_AT TODO"
        line_clean = line.strip()
        if line_clean.startswith('- '):
            line_clean = line_clean[2:]
        # Split by " BY " to get title and artist part
        parts = line_clean.split(' BY ')
        if len(parts) == 2:
            title = parts[0].strip()
            artists_str = parts[1].strip()
            # Remove the " RELEASED_AT TODO" from artists_str
            artists_str = artists_str.replace(' RELEASED_AT TODO', '').strip()
            todo_songs.append({'title': title, 'artists': artists_str})

# Build the updated content by replacing each "RELEASED_AT TODO" with the correct date.
lines = note_content.split('\n')
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title: line starts with "- " and then song title before " BY "
        # Example: "- Silver Lining BY Ava Morgan RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # We'll split on " BY " to get the song title part.
        parts = line.split(' BY ')
        # parts[0] is "- Silver Lining" (with leading dash and space)
        song_title = parts[0].strip('- ').strip()
        # Get the date from mapping
        date = song_release_dates.get(song_title)
        if date:
            # Replace "RELEASED_AT TODO" with the date
            line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', date)
        else:
            print(f"Warning: No date found for {song_title}")
    new_lines.append(line)
new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

# We have the note content. Let's build a mapping of song titles to release dates (MM/YYYY) based on the confirmed dates.
release_dates = {
    "Silver Lining": "12/2022",
    "Walking Through the Valley of Shadows": "08/2022",
    "Where Shadows Come to Life": "01/2023",
    "Eternal Melancholy": "04/2023",
    "Crimson Veil": "01/2020",
    "Elusive Joy": "03/2021",
    "Ephemeral Beauty": "01/2020",
    "Stardust Serenade": "04/2019",
    "Veiled Behind a Mask of Joy": "10/2022",
    "In the Wake of Unspoken Promises": "07/2022",
    "Wading Through the Ashes of Love": "09/2020",
    "Fading Like a Distant Star": "01/2019",
    "Wilted Grace": "01/2022"
}

# Get the current content from the note we just fetched.
current_content = apis.simple_note.show_note(note_id=3084, access_token=simple_note_token)["content"]

# Split into lines and replace TODO for each line that has a matching song.
lines = current_content.split("\n")
updated_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if "TODO" in line:
        # Extract song title: line starts with "- " and then " BY " separates title and artist.
        # Example: "- Silver Lining BY Ava Morgan RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # We can find the part between "- " and " BY ".
        if line.startswith("- "):
            title_part = line[2:].split(" BY ")[0]
            if title_part in release_dates:
                line = line.replace("TODO", release_dates[title_part])
    updated_lines.append(line)

updated_content = "\n".join(updated_lines)
print(updated_content)

# Loop until no liked songs remain in the queue
while True:
    # Get current queue
    queue = apis.spotify.show_song_queue(access_token=access_token)
    # Find first liked song in the queue
    found = None
    for song in queue:
        if song['song_id'] in liked_ids:
            found = song
            break
    if found is None:
        break
    # Remove it by its current position
    pos = found['position']
    print(f"Removing song_id {found['song_id']} at position {pos}")
    result = apis.spotify.remove_song_from_queue(access_token=access_token, position=pos)
